raceStillReproduces.method: Static architecture trace of the abort/rebind/serialization paths in the pure-upstream Remote arch (read-only; no mutating tests run, consistent with hands-off constraints). Cross-checked against B-DA1 diagnosis, d5-upstream-impact.md line 14, and the current source.
raceStillReproduces.evidence: The B-DA1 race mechanism is INTACT and only HALF-fixed under the Remote arch. Findings: (1) recompose() remains a pure synchronous scope re-link — packages/preset/agent-presets/src/index.ts:650 -> binding.rebind() -> packages/core/scope/src/index.ts:78 linkScopeParent -> scopeParents.set() (a WeakMap write, zero side effects, no disposal). This confirms B-DA1's Hypothesis-A refutation still holds: recompose does NOT cancel the agent. (2) The three-and-only-three abort sources are unchanged: machine.cancel({kind:'disposed'}) at packages/core/agent-loop/src/index.ts:591 (agent disposal); agent.cancel({kind:'user'},{keepInbox:true}) at packages/api/session-controller/src/commands.ts:486 (session.cancel RPC); agent.cancel({kind:'hook'...}) at packages/data/phase-gate/src/phase-gate.ts:897 (300s stall watchdog, impossible on first message). The @Remote('select') handler never calls agent.cancel — so the abort, when it fires on first turn, is disposal from a fiber-lifecycle edge, exactly as B-DA1 concluded. (3) THE CRITICAL GAP: the original apiproxy fix had TWO halves (d5 line 14): (a) swapPreset synchronous slot reservation + recompose awaits queued (:3024), and (b) the TURN PATH `await pendingSwitch` so prompts wait for in-flight switches (:2397). Under the Remote arch, ONLY half (a) was re-homed — the private `switches` Map in AgentPresets (:684, :697-704) serializes select-vs-select. Half (b) is GONE: packages/api/session-controller/src/commands.ts:294 prompt() resolves the agent and dispatches (agent.steer/agent.followup) with NO await of any in-flight preset switch. The `switches` Map is `private` (agent-presets/src/index.ts:684) with no cross-package accessor, so session-controller physically cannot await it. git grep for pendingSwitch/switches.get/awaitSwitch/drain across session-controller src = zero hits. (4) Because JS is single-threaded, the synchronous rebind cannot interleave a synchronous chain walk (scopeChainOf/scopeTarget) — so the race only manifests when a standing-mount observer's chain read spans an await and re-reads scopeParents after the rebind (the d5 comment: 'a mid-flight rebind destabilizes the agent's scope observers'). That await-spanning observer path still exists in dsh-scope + the standing-mount lifecycle and is now REACHABLE because prompt and select are unserialized across two separate services. Test coverage confirms the gap: packages/preset/agent-presets/tests/remote.spec.ts:380 tests select-vs-select serialization and :399 the agent-preset/locked guard, but there is NO test for the actual B-DA1 scenario (concurrent select + prompt / switch racing turn-start). NOTE: I could not obtain a live session-JSONL turn/end.reason.reason.kind ('disposed' vs 'error') capture — the definitive runtime confirmation B-DA1 asked for remains unproduced; the reproduction is established by architecture trace, not by a captured trajectory, so residual uncertainty on whether the field abort is 'disposed' vs an orthogonal LLM 'error' (Hypothesis B) persists.

architecturalRecommend.observerDesc: Make the data-agent scope observers rebind-safe so a mid-flight scope-parent rebind cannot destabilize an in-flight turn's chain walk, and re-home the prompt-side serialization into the data-agent layer. Concretely: (1) In the data-agent-scoped wrapper packages/data/preset-autojoin (or a small new da plugin), restore the missing 'half (b)': before a turn's first step admits (agent/pre-step hook, which preset-autojoin already has the agent/created seam to reach), await any in-flight preset switch for that session — the equivalent of the deleted apiproxy turnAgentFor `await pendingSwitch` (:2397). Since AgentPresets.switches is private, expose a narrow, additive read-only accessor on AgentPresets (e.g. `pendingSwitch(sessionId): Promise<unknown> | undefined`) that the da hook awaits — this keeps the generic upstream @Remote('select') untouched and puts the coupling in the data-agent seam. (2) Optionally harden the standing-mount observer so any chain walk that spans an await snapshots the parent chain up-front (or reads under a rebind-guard) rather than re-reading scopeParents after a yield. This keeps the fix in the fork's data-agent surface, matching d5's fix-sketch branch (b) 'scope-observer rebind-fragility belongs in the data-agent layer so upstream preset-swap serialization stays as-is.'
architecturalRecommend.remoteSerializationDesc: Rework the preset-swap sequence at the Remote/gateway layer so the whole switch is serialized against the turn lifecycle upstream: extend the @Remote('select') / session-controller prompt boundary so that (a) a select reserves a per-session slot synchronously before any await, and (b) the session-controller prompt() handler (packages/api/session-controller/src/commands.ts:294) awaits that slot before dispatching agent.steer/followup — i.e. re-home BOTH halves of the original apiproxy fix into the generic Remote packages (agent-presets + session-controller). This would require session-controller to depend on / query agent-presets switch state (a new cross-generic-package coupling) and changes upstream-shared concurrency control.
architecturalRecommend.rationale: observer-fix wins on four grounds. (1) Locality of blame: d5 line 14 explicitly diagnosed the driver as 'a mid-flight rebind destabilizes the agent's scope OBSERVERS' — a data-agent scopeId concern — and prescribed branch (b) 'make data-agent observers rebind-safe so upstream preset-swap serialization stays as-is' UNLESS the race is proven in pure upstream. It is NOT proven in pure upstream: the select-side serialization already shipped generically and passes its tests; only the data-agent-specific observer fragility + the missing prompt-await remain. (2) Minimal upstream drift: Remote-serialization forces session-controller (generic) to couple to agent-presets switch state, creating exactly the kind of fork-vs-upstream divergence the whole UM* phase is trying to eliminate; observer-fix confines the coupling to the da-scoped preset-autojoin wrapper (which already legitimately hooks agent lifecycle). (3) The clean seam already exists: preset-autojoin is the documented da §4.2 wrapper on agent/created, and a narrow additive accessor on AgentPresets is a smaller, more auditable change than reworking the shared prompt/select boundary. (4) Reversibility/risk: if a future pure-upstream repro emerges, the select-half is already generic and the prompt-await can be promoted upstream later; starting data-agent-local is the lower-regret path. Caveat: the definitive JSONL 'disposed' confirmation is still missing, so whichever path is taken must first capture a real turn/end reason to rule out the orthogonal Hypothesis-B (LLM 'error') before declaring B-DA1 fully resolved.

implementationSketch: Scope 3 (Scope 2 already done at 025db697ab).
